source.title: Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("But Few Contests": county council nominations, with labels); members confirmed by the Lurgan Times, 7 June 1902, p. 3 ("Armagh County Council": complete list of the elected members)
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: names and labels read from the page images; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1902: polled 28 May 1902 in six divisions; the other fifteen divisions (seventeen seats) were returned unopposed. Returned unopposed. Retiring member ("old member"); no label printed. William Byers: no party label printed in 1902. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Markethill, 6 April 1899, printed 'U': Lurgan Mail, 15 April 1899, p. 6 ("Election Results: Armagh Co. Council Returns"); party labels from the Northern Star, 15 April 1899, p. 5, and the Portadown News, 15 April 1899, p. 8; figures checked against those two and the Portadown News, 8 April 1899, p. 5; Markethill, 27 May 1908, printed 'U.': Northern Whig, 6 June 1908, p. 10 ("Provincial Elections: County Councils: Armagh"); candidates in the Newry Reporter, 2 May 1908, p. 10 ("Armagh County Council": the nominations)).
